intro_script: Welcome to your daily Robotics News Digest for November 16, 2026. We've got 14 updates, including Gemini's new dexterity, OpenAI's shift in focus, and DHL's warehouse AI pilots. Tune in for the latest.
outro_script: And that’s all the circuits for today! Hope your day is as smoothly programmed as Gemini Robotics 2.5. Until tomorrow, keep those algorithms humming! Bye for now!

items.title: Google DeepMind launches Gemini Robotics 2.5 with improved dexterity and industrial capabilities
items.summary: Google DeepMind launched Gemini Robotics 2.5, an updated vision-language-action model to enhance robots' ability to perform complex physical tasks. The new model improved dexterity, reliability, and safety across over 200 tasks, achieving success rates 30 to 100 percent higher and completing operations 20 to 30 percent faster. Demonstrations involved Apptronik's Apollo 2 humanoid robot successfully performing automotive kitting on Mercedes-Benz production lines. Safety improvements were also integrated, with new controls increasing safe task completion around obstacles and people. The development also introduced ASIMOV-Jailbreak and used the Gemini 4 Argon model to generate training scenarios, accelerating robotics research.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, Google DeepMind launches Gemini Robotics 2.5 with improved dexterity and industrial capabilities. This report details the release of an updated vision-language-action model designed to enhance robots' capacity for complex physical tasks through advancements in dexterity, reliability, and safety. The new model demonstrated success rates 30 to 100 percent higher and completed operations 20 to 30 percent faster across more than two hundred tasks. Demonstrations included the Apptronik Apollo 2 humanoid robot successfully executing automotive kitting operations on Mercedes-Benz production lines. Safety enhancements were incorporated through new controls that increased safe task completion around obstacles and personnel. Furthermore, the development incorporated ASIMOV-Jailbreak and utilized the Gemini 4 Argon model to generate training scenarios, thereby accelerating robotics research. This advancement signals a significant step forward in integrating advanced AI into practical industrial automation.

items.title: OpenAI disbands robotics team, folds work into core research
items.summary: OpenAI disbanded its robotics team and integrated its staff into the main research and applied organizations to accelerate robotics development. This restructuring stems from the finding that general purpose frontier models can be applied directly to robotics, prompting a shift from the previous research approach. The company is currently developing its own humanoid robot, aiming for a public demonstration in 2027. This move challenges the view that robot intelligence requires a separate model development organization. Some experts argue that general intelligence models can complement real-world robot experience rather than entirely replacing it.
items.audio_script: From Humanoid.guide, "OpenAI disbands robotics team, folds work into core research". This report details OpenAI's restructuring of its robotics focus by integrating the team's work into core research and applied organizations following a shift in research methodology. The company determined that general purpose frontier models can be directly applied to robotics, leading to the dissolution of the specialized robotics team. This restructuring reflects a move away from a separate development approach toward leveraging existing large models for robotics tasks. OpenAI is now focusing development internally on a humanoid robot, with a target for a public demonstration in 2027. This development challenges the premise that robotics requires entirely separate model development. The implications suggest that general intelligence models can augment real-world robot experience. Industry focus will now be on the practical application and integration of advanced models in physical systems.

items.title: DHL Supply Chain pilots adaptive robotics and AI orchestration in warehouse operations
items.summary: DHL Supply Chain is piloting adaptive AI-powered robots and AI orchestration to coordinate robotics, AI, and human workers across its global logistics network. This initiative is part of the Intelligent Supply Chain framework, focusing on coordinating entire warehouse workflows rather than just automating individual tasks. Adaptive robots adjust actions based on changing conditions, complemented by AI orchestration software connecting employees, equipment, and data. The testing involves systems that dynamically allocate resources based on order volumes to improve throughput and flexibility. DHL views the combination of physical AI (controlling machinery) and digital AI (analyzing information) as essential for creating an efficient and resilient supply chain with human expertise.

The testing involved systems dynamically allocating resources according to order volumes to enhance throughput and flexibility. This approach integrates physical AI controlling machinery with digital AI analyzing information to foster an efficient and resilient supply chain with human expertise. This development signals a trend toward holistic operational management in logistics driven by integrated physical and digital intelligence.

items.title: Zacua Ventures raises $135 million to invest in robotics, physical AI and industrial technology
items.summary: Zacua Ventures raised $135 million for its second fund, focusing on robotics, physical AI, and industrial technologies. This fund more than doubled the original $56 million fund, attracting commitments from over 30 investors globally. The firm is expanding its focus beyond construction to encompass the broader "Physical Industries" like manufacturing and energy. Zacua has already invested in companies like Gravis Robotics and Origin Robotics, demonstrating its interest in industrial automation. The firm leverages its network to provide portfolio companies with access to industrial customers and operational testing environments.

items.title: Avride reaches one million robot deliveries as network expands across US
items.summary: Avride has completed one million robot deliveries across the United States as it expands into urban neighborhoods and university campuses. The company reported 180,000 deliveries in October and currently handles a daily volume of 7,000 deliveries. Avride operates in over 30 U.S. markets, including cities like Austin and Miami. The robots integrate with platforms such as Uber Eats and Grubhub, enabling customers to order food. Growth is attributed to coordination among internal teams and commercial partners, with plans for continued expansion.

The operation spans over thirty United States markets, including metropolitan areas such as Austin and Miami. These robotic units interface with existing food delivery platforms like Uber Eats and Grubhub to facilitate customer ordering. Growth in delivery volume is credited to coordination between internal teams and commercial partners, with further expansion planned. This development indicates continued integration of autonomous systems into consumer logistics infrastructure.

items.title: Wing and Walmart launch drone delivery service in Memphis
items.summary: Wing and Walmart launched drone delivery service in the Memphis area, expanding autonomous delivery to Tennessee and Arkansas. Eligible customers can order groceries and essentials from Walmart with delivery times as fast as 30 minutes. The initial service covers neighborhoods around Walmart Supercenters in Bartlett, Cordova, and West Memphis. This expansion is part of a larger goal to reach nearly 20 US metropolitan areas by 2027. The service utilizes drones up to 60 mph and aims to make drone delivery a practical alternative for time-sensitive purchases.

The initial service deployment covers neighborhoods surrounding Walmart Supercenters located in Bartlett, Cordova, and West Memphis, marking an expansion of autonomous delivery into Tennessee and Arkansas. The system employs drones capable of speeds up to sixty miles per hour, designed to provide a practical alternative for time-sensitive purchases. items.title: Serve Robotics opens autonomous delivery network to developers and businesses
items.summary: Serve Robotics has launched an AV Delivery Developer Portal, allowing developers and businesses to programmatically summon robots from its autonomous sidewalk delivery fleet. This portal includes a public API and a sandbox environment for testing before using live robots. The platform enables applications, businesses, and AI assistants to integrate these robots for last-mile delivery and other tasks. Serve manages the complex operations of dispatch, routing, navigation, and supervision for these deliveries. This innovation aims to make on-demand delivery affordable and integrate physical robotics into everyday workflows.

items.title: Welcome, Dyna-2.1!
items.summary: Dyna 2.1 is a software foundation model for robotics developed by DYNA Robotics in California. It is categorized within the intelligence layer of a robotic system, distinguishing it from physical hardware. The model has a Humanoid Guide Brain Score of 8 out of 10, placing it in the state of the art band. Release is scheduled for September 29, 2026, and the product is currently available on backorder. Buyers should assess the software's performance based on specific deployment requirements rather than mechanical specifications.

items.title: Welcome, GR RL!
items.summary: GR RL is a robot foundation model developed by ByteDance Seed, building upon the GR 3 vision language action model. It addresses the challenge of noisy human demonstrations by combining demonstration training with reinforcement learning through subsequent robot practice. The training involves three stages: filtering poor demonstrations, mirroring retained examples, and introducing practice guided by results. This research focuses on refining how robot policies are trained rather than producing a physical robot product. The model is assessed as developing, reflecting its focus on the quality of learning methods in robotics.

items.title: LG partners with KIRIA on humanoid safety before 2027 debut
items.summary: LG Electronics partnered with KIRIA to develop safety, reliability, and usability assessments for humanoid robots before their planned 2027 debut. The collaboration involves LG developing testing infrastructure and contributing to national and international safety standards at KIRIA's Humanoid Robot Safety Certification Center. The partnership aims to identify key challenges like collision avoidance and motion stability for robots operating in shared human spaces. This safety verification effort supports LG's development of a bipedal robot slated for unveiling in early 2027. LG is integrating hardware, intelligence, and operational data into its robotics program.

This partnership focuses on identifying critical challenges such as collision avoidance and motion stability for robots operating in shared human spaces through rigorous verification efforts. The process involves LG integrating hardware, intelligence, and operational data into its robotics program to ensure safety compliance. The work establishes a framework for regulatory oversight in the evolving humanoid robotics sector.

items.title: Robbyant launches LingBot-Touch to give robots a sense of touch
items.summary: Robbyant released LingBot-Touch, an open-source tactile foundation model enabling robots to perceive touch by unifying data from magnetic, visual, and piezoresistive sensing. This unified architecture translates diverse sensor signals into a shared fingertip coordinate space, allowing different hands and action models to share tactile understanding. Integrating LingBot-Touch resulted in significant performance improvements, with action models achieving 14 to 26 percentage point gains in real-world manipulation tasks. The model is designed to be reusable across different sensors and dexterous hands, accommodating future hardware iterations.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, Robbyant launches LingBot-Touch to give robots a sense of touch. The LingBot-Touch architecture translates these diverse sensor signals into a shared fingertip coordinate space, facilitating shared tactile understanding across different hands and action models. Integration of this model resulted in substantial performance enhancements, with action models demonstrating gains ranging from fourteen to twenty-six percentage points in real-world manipulation tasks. The model is engineered for reusability across various sensors and dexterous hands, accommodating future hardware evolution. This development signals a significant step toward more nuanced and adaptable robotic interaction capabilities.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: Runtime governability in ROS 2: where should changing operating conditions be handled?
items.summary: The author seeks architectural experience regarding how to handle changes in external operating conditions while a ROS 2 system is actively performing a task. ROS 2's existing mechanisms for lifecycle management and recovery are considered sufficient, and the focus is on where to represent and evaluate this changing context. Potential locations for this context include the task layer, a supervisory component, or external services. The author asks specific questions about context ownership, handling source unavailability, and introducing higher-level logic without compromising local safety. The discussion centers on the concept of "runtime governability" in autonomous systems.
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Runtime governability in ROS 2: where should changing operating conditions be handled?". This story examines the architectural considerations for managing shifts in external operating conditions within active ROS 2 systems, focusing on where this dynamic context should be represented and evaluated. The discussion explored whether existing ROS 2 lifecycle management mechanisms are sufficient and investigated potential locations for context representation, including the task layer, a supervisory component, or external services. Specific inquiries addressed context ownership, the handling of source unavailability, and the introduction of higher-level logic while maintaining local safety guarantees, centering on the concept of runtime governability in autonomous systems. This research provides guidance for designing more robust and adaptable autonomous software architectures.

items.title: Why Skydio Built a Lopsided Drone
items.summary: The Skydio F10 Lightrunner is a fixed-wing camera drone featuring asymmetrical wings to accommodate a wingtip camera payload. This design necessitated uneven motor placement to balance thrust against the added drag from the camera. Engineers used modeling and optimization to achieve a viable design that balanced the camera, lift, and control requirements. The drone utilizes model predictive control to autonomously manage transitions between hovering and high-speed flight. A MegaDock system allows for the autonomous launch, recovery, and recharging of up to five F10 drones.
items.audio_script: From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Why Skydio Built a Lopsided Drone". This story details the engineering process behind the Skydio F10 Lightrunner, which is a fixed-wing camera drone featuring asymmetrical wings designed to accommodate a wingtip camera payload. Engineers achieved this design through modeling and optimization to balance the camera, lift, and control requirements, necessitating uneven motor placement to counteract the increased drag. The system utilizes model predictive control to autonomously manage transitions between hovering and high-speed flight, and it incorporates a MegaDock system for the autonomous management of up to five drones. This work demonstrates advanced control methods for complex aerodynamic systems. Future developments in autonomous aerial systems will likely build upon these advancements in control and payload integration.

items.title: Racing the Clock: Teaching VLNs Budget-Conditioned Object Search
items.summary: The research investigates budget-conditioned object search for vision-language-navigation (VLN) models, where agents must find target instances within a specific action budget. The study compares supervising VLNs with a privileged Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP) expert versus a room-level Bellman expert. Despite the TSP expert showing better routing performance, the Bellman-supervised VLN consistently outperforms it in learning exploration under partial observability. This suggests that effective exploration supervision should focus on decisions under partial observability rather than imitating fully known optimal routes. Experiments show the Bellman-supervised VLN finds a higher percentage of reachable targets compared to the other methods.

items.title: Learning Latent Goal Costs for Visual World-Model Planning with an Expanding Curriculum
items.summary: Image-goal planning with frozen visual world models benefits from learning latent goal costs. A residual adapter is fitted onto frozen I-JEPA embeddings to improve this latent goal cost signal. Planners collect trajectories from expanding regions to learn from successful and failed rollouts without task-specific labels. Experiments on DotWall and PointMaze showed success rates increasing from 54% to 98% and 82% to 96%, respectively. This demonstrates that planning experience can refine a frozen visual representation's goal cost.

items.title: Talk to Act: A Synthetic Multi-Turn Dialogue Benchmark for Human Intent Extraction and Action Planning in Robotics
items.summary: A synthetic multi-turn dialogue dataset is introduced to benchmark human intent extraction and action planning in human-robot interaction. The work frames intent extraction as a tool-calling problem, testing small language models (270M to 8B parameters) on these tasks without task-specific fine-tuning. Results indicate that these compact models achieve reasonable performance in intent extraction and action planning. This suggests that smaller, locally deployable models offer a useful baseline for conversational robotic systems. Further fine-tuning and more realistic data are anticipated to improve performance for real-world applications.

items.title: Grounding Object-to-Object Hazard Reasoning into 3D Risk Fields for Task-Conditioned Safety
items.summary: A framework based on vision-language models infers task- and scene-dependent safety constraints for robot manipulation by analyzing object interactions. It uses RGB-D observations and natural language instructions to determine if a task should be rejected or to identify preventable object-pair hazards. Open-vocabulary segmentation and depth information are then used to map detected objects into 3D and construct continuous risk fields representing hazardous regions. These risk fields are integrated with an obstacle avoidance module to correct robot motions during execution. The system is evaluated on preventable hazards, rejected tasks, and safe variants in both simulation and real-world settings.

items.title: Natural Swing-Up of an Underpowered Double Pendulum
items.summary: Robots with weak motors should utilize their natural dynamics instead of resisting them. The research explores swinging up a direct-drive planar two-link robot whose motors provide only 6% of the shoulder gravity torque. Energy injection is analyzed by splitting the input torque into a power-neutral steering component and a scalar pumping input that changes energy. A linear program is used to allocate this torque to maximize pumping subject to torque limits and a control-Lyapunov constraint. Experiments confirmed swing-ups along the natural modes and compared different allocation strategies.

items.title: X-Nav Technical Report: Real-World Long-Horizon Indoor-to-Outdoor Navigation on a Humanoid Robot
items.summary: X-Nav presents a system for long-horizon indoor-to-outdoor navigation for humanoid robots based on language instructions. It utilizes a data engine to collect navigation data and a navigation model, MELIOR, to predict actions or navigation goals from RGB images. The agentic workflow, X-Navarch, translates human instructions into sub-tasks, using MELIOR for target navigation and obstacle avoidance. The system successfully navigated a mission of about a hundred meters by adapting the model with data from digital twins. MELIOR also achieves competitive results on established navigation benchmarks.

items.title: On the Utility of Pre-Trained Visual Representations for Policy Learning of Contact-Rich Insertion Tasks
items.summary: Visuomotor imitation learning is data-inefficient and brittle to visual shifts, suggesting pre-trained visual representations could help policy learning. The study investigates this by comparing representations from vision foundation models against explicit contact-centric representations for insertion tasks. Testing across controlled perturbations showed that task dependence is more subtle than previously thought, with different representations performing differently even on nearly identical tasks. Results indicate that spatially-grounded, contact-centric information is distinctly valuable for contact-rich policy learning. This work motivates further research into contact perception for visuomotor policy learning.

items.title: AI-guided robotic in situ fabrication of curvature- and tissue-adaptive wireless bioelectronics
items.summary: An AI-guided robotic in situ fabrication platform is presented for creating wireless wound electrotherapy devices directly onto transparent wound dressings. The system employs AI for wound segmentation to determine geometry and tissue curvature, which are then incorporated into the electromagnetic design of the receiving coils. This method accounts for both anatomical curvature and tissue dielectric loading to correct for shifts in resonant behavior. A printable silver ink was used to fabricate these multilayer wireless devices on curved materials. The work establishes a framework for geometry-adaptive wireless bioelectronics through a perception-to-design-to-fabrication process.
